title: PH versus PSPACE
formal: Is \(\mathrm{PH}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\)? Equivalently, is there a fixed integer \(k\ge 0\) such that the truth problem for fully quantified Boolean formulas belongs to \(\Sigma ^{p}_{k}\)?
why: Separates unbounded polynomial-space computation from a bounded number of polynomial-time alternations.

progress.text: The cited textbook draft states TQBF completeness, \(\mathrm{PH}\subseteq \mathrm{PSPACE}\) and the collapse consequence of equality.
New multilevel optimization completeness theorems preserve the bounded-level versus PSPACE classification without separating the classes.
A sparse-oracle construction separates PH from PSPACE while allowing PH to collapse; the result is explicitly relativized.

references.locator: Discovery source; retrieved 2026-09-11. Evidence locator: PH is contained

definitions: Languages are subsets of \(\{0,1\}\)*. PSPACE contains the languages decided by deterministic Turing machines that halt on every input of length n while using at most \(C(n+1)^{a}\) work-tape cells, for constants C,a depending on the machine. The read-only input tape is not charged, and there is no polynomial time limit. Set \(\Sigma ^{p}_{0}=\mathrm{P}\), the deterministic polynomial-time languages. For \(k\ge 1, a\) language L lies in \(\Sigma ^{p}_{k}\) if there are a deterministic polynomial-time predicate R and a polynomial p such that \(x\in \mathrm{L}\) exactly when \(\exists y_{1}\forall y_{2}\exists y_{3}\cdots Q_{k} y_{k} R(x,y_{1},\ldots ,y_{k})=1\), where each \(y_{i}\) ranges over \(\{0,1\}^{p(|x|)}\) and \(Q_{k}\) is existential for odd k and universal for even k. Set \(\mathrm{PH}=\bigcup _{k\ge 0}\Sigma ^{p}_{k}\). The integer k is fixed for an entire language; it cannot grow with an input. Machines and predicates are uniform and have no advice or oracle. A fully quantified Boolean formula is an explicit Boolean formula using AND, OR and NOT, preceded by quantifiers binding every variable exactly once; variable names and the entire formula are binary encoded. Its truth uses the ordinary successive quantifier semantics over \(\{0,1\}\). The language TQBF consists of its true well-formed encodings; malformed strings are rejected. The number of quantifier blocks in TQBF inputs is unrestricted.
answer_criterion: A positive resolution proves \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\subseteq \mathrm{PH}\); the reverse inclusion is already known. Equivalently it places TQBF in one fixed \(\Sigma ^{p}_{k}\), which would put every PSPACE language in that same level by polynomial-time reductions. A negative resolution proves that some PSPACE language, equivalently TQBF, is outside every fixed level. A separation at one fixed level or an oracle-relative result alone does not answer the question.

context_blocks.title: What is being compared?
context_blocks.text: Polynomial space lets a computation reuse a bounded amount of memory for a potentially very long time. The polynomial hierarchy instead organizes efficiently checked conditions by a fixed number of alternating existential and universal choices. For example, an existential block asks for a witness, a following universal block checks every challenge to it, and another existential block can give a response depending on that challenge. The question asks whether any polynomial-space computation can be expressed with a fixed number of such blocks.

context_blocks.title: Order of choices matters
context_blocks.text: The formula \(\forall x\exists y (x=y)\) is true: after the value of x is fixed, y can take the same value. The formula \(\exists y\forall x (x=y)\) is false because one bit cannot equal both possible values of x. Thus replacing a sequence of dependent choices by one initial guess changes the problem. A formula with arbitrarily many alternating choices describes a potentially long strategy, even though testing its final Boolean condition is straightforward.

context_blocks.title: Why polynomial space is enough
context_blocks.text: A quantified formula can be evaluated by recursively trying the two values of each variable and combining the answers according to its quantifier. The procedure reuses memory after finishing each branch; it need not store the exponentially large game tree. TQBF is PSPACE-complete. The standard alternation theorem also identifies polynomial-time alternating computation, with no fixed bound on its number of alternations, with PSPACE. Neither characterization shows that an arbitrary number of rounds compresses to a constant.

context_blocks.title: A union of levels has a subtle consequence
context_blocks.text: The definition of PH initially lets different languages use different fixed numbers of blocks. Nevertheless, equality with PSPACE would imply one common finite level containing all of PSPACE: TQBF would belong to some \(\Sigma ^{p}_{k}\) and every PSPACE language reduces to it. Therefore \(\mathrm{PH}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\) would collapse the hierarchy. Conversely, proving that the hierarchy has infinitely many distinct levels would separate it from PSPACE. A separation \(\mathrm{PH}\ne \mathrm{PSPACE}\) alone does not establish that every hierarchy level is distinct; this is why the card differs from the non-collapse question.

context_blocks.title: What later results do and do not show
context_blocks.text: Grüne, Johannes, Orlin and Wulf’s February 2026 results make many multilevel optimization problems complete for individual hierarchy levels or for PSPACE. Completeness locates the problems within the classes; it does not prove the classes different. Egidy’s 2026 oracle construction illustrates another distinction: relative to that oracle, PH collapses while remaining strictly below PSPACE. This is a statement in a model with an additional oracle, rather than a resolution for ordinary machines. Historical preprints claim equality or non-collapse, but the sources checked here do not establish either as a settled theorem. The review did not independently audit those claimed proofs.

sentences: Does every polynomial-space decision problem lie in the polynomial hierarchy?
PH allows a fixed number of alternating quantifier blocks for each language.
PSPACE also describes polynomial-time alternation with no fixed bound on the number of alternations.
Equality would put TQBF in one finite level and hence collapse PH to that level.
Completeness and oracle results illuminate the distinction without settling the ordinary class equality.
